narrative.overview:
The README is an operating handbook written the way a real one is: for a type, and flight-tested on one airframe. The type is every Mac with Apple silicon flying Star Citizen offline; the airframe is the one machine it has run on, a MacBook Pro 16-inch with an M4 Pro and 24 GB. The line under the title names the type, the data plate names the airframe (TESTED ON), and every figure with numbers says whose numbers they are. It documents the machine the way pilots document an aircraft, with a cover that carries a data plate, numbered sections on thumb tabs, limitations, emergency and normal procedures as challenge-and-response checklists, and performance figures that state their conditions. The light theme is the printed page, ink on paper. The dark theme is the instrument face, light markings on a dark ground.

The surface is github.com, so the system has exactly two layers. GitHub owns everything Markdown renders: the body face and its sizes, heading sizes and their rules, table borders and striping, code-block grounds and their monospace face, link colour, alert colours and icons, the column width and every breakpoint. None of those are tokens here and none may be overridden. The project owns the SVG figures in `docs/assets/`, drawn by `docs/assets/src/build.py`, and the conventions for how Markdown is written. Every token in this file is a value in that script; the figures' two palettes are GitHub's own light and dark page colours, so a figure sits on the page as if printed on it.

Lettering in figures is Helvetica and Courier converted to outlines, because an SVG shown through an image tag cannot load fonts. One image file serves desktop and phone, so lettering is sized for the phone: the cover is shown at about 0.41 of its drawn size there and a figure at 0.6, which puts the smallest lettering at about 10 px.
keyCharacteristics: Ink and paper, plus an instrument-marking code (green, yellow, red) that appears only where it encodes a measurement or a limit.
Two faces with fixed jobs: Helvetica Bold capitals name things, Courier states data.
Square, flat, ruled. No shadows, no gradients, no rounded containers.
Every figure exists as a light and a dark file, chosen by the reader's colour scheme.
Checklists set in 38 monospace columns with dot leaders, so they fit a phone without wrapping.
Static. The one moving element is the take-off sequence, a recording.

rules.name: The Marking Code Rule
rules.body: Green, yellow and red are instrument markings, not accents. A colour may appear in a figure only where it encodes a measured range, a target or a limit, and the figure must say in words what it means (GREEN: 25 AND ABOVE, RED LINE: TEST MACHINE, 24 GB). Everything else is ink on paper.

rules.name: The Two Reds Rule
rules.body: Limit Red marks a number the machine cannot exceed. Emergency Red marks Section 3 and only Section 3: its tab and the hatched rule under its heading. Neither is used for emphasis.

rules.name: The One Tint Rule
rules.body: Ink at 0.38 opacity has a single meaning: the measured spread at the end of a bar, where the true value lies somewhere inside. A dashed ink outline with no fill means not in memory or not part of the kit's result (data in swap, the as-found row). No other tints or fills exist.

rules.name: The One Size Rule
rules.body: Inside a figure every piece of lettering is 17. Hierarchy comes from face, weight, capitals and ink against muted, never from a second size. The cover is the only plate with a scale, and its smallest lettering is 24.

rules.name: The Phone Floor Rule
rules.body: Lettering is sized by what it becomes in a 360 px column: drawn size times 0.6 for a figure, times 0.41 for the cover, and the result stays at about 10 px. A new figure keeps the 600 measure and the 17 lettering rather than adding detail that needs smaller type.

rules.name: The Outline Rule
rules.body: Every letter in a figure is a path produced by `textpath` from Helvetica or Courier. No `<text>` elements, no font references, so each figure carries its full reading in the `aria-label` and `<title>` and again in the `alt` of the image.

rules.name: The Written Range Rule
rules.body: A measured range is written with the word "to" (16 to 25 FPS), in prose, tables and figures alike. An en dash in a table cell means not measured.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: One blue (`launcher-accent`) marks the action a person can take now and the progress of what is under way: the primary button, the bar's fill, the running step, the busy dot, the switch that is on, and in its lighter step the focus ring. There is no second accent, and blue never says that something is good or bad.

rules.name: The State Colour Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red only say what state something is in. Green: ready, done, in flight, a frame rate at or above the target. Amber: the person's turn, a frame rate below the target, memory past what this Mac has installed. Red: a failure, the game stopped, the armed Stop. Each stands beside words that say the same thing, and none is decoration.

rules.name: The Solid Fill Rule
rules.body: Nothing of the backdrop shows through a control, a box or a pane. Everything laid on the hero has an opaque fill: the buttons, the tag, the bar's track, the setup pane, both notices. The title and the status line stand on the backdrop itself, behind a veil that darkens it from the left and from below. No blur and no glass. The white tints (`launcher-hover`, `launcher-selected`, `launcher-switch-off`) are used only over the rail and the ground, never over the picture.

rules.name: The Three Small Steps Rule
rules.body: All running interface text is 12, 13 or 15. 13 is the default, 12 is for notes and states, 15 is for a line that leads: the status line, a large button, a row's heading, the tagline. Above them are three sizes with one job each: 20 for a tile's value, 22 for a page title, 44 for the game's name. Inside a step, hierarchy comes from weight (400, 500, 600, 650, 700) and from text against muted against faint.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Everything is in sentence case at normal tracking. Capitals are not a style here and no label is tracked out. Negative tracking belongs only to the four largest settings: the brand at 15, the tile value at 20, the page title at 22 and the title at 44.

rules.name: The Tabular Numerals Rule
rules.body: Any number that can change while a person watches is set in tabular numerals, so the line does not shift: the figure at the right of the status line, the note under the bar, tile values and notes, step states, the count in the sidebar, the version.

rules.name: The Said Once Rule
rules.body: The status line says the state once: a dot, one sentence, one figure at its right. Nothing else on the page repeats that sentence. The command a person needs is on the primary button and is not repeated in the notice beside it.

rules.name: The Source On This Mac Rule
rules.body: No number without a source on this Mac. Every figure the launcher shows is read from the machine it runs on, or says where it was measured. A reading that does not exist yet is an en dash, never an estimate. Opened without the app, the page says "Simulated readings." in front of the line that names the one Mac measured, and the version reads "simulator".

rules.name: The Own Picture Rule
rules.body: The launcher carries no imagery, logo or interface styling of the game. The backdrop is a photograph: one of three from NASA's open archives that come with the app, each credited on the panel, or a picture the person chose, which stays on their Mac. Nothing on it is drawn or generated.

rules.name: The Corrected In Place Rule
rules.body: When the engine reports, a row, a tile or a control is corrected where it stands. Nothing is rebuilt and nothing moves without cause; the row that needs the person is scrolled into view.

rules.name: The Reveal Rule
rules.body: The bar's fill always spans the whole track and is revealed with a clip-path over 0.5 s. It is never resized, so its two colours stay where they belong on the scale.

rules.name: The At Rest In Flight Rule
rules.body: While the game runs, nothing animates and nothing transitions: every transition and animation in the window is switched off for the flight phase, because the game needs the machine. Readings still change; they change in place.

dos: Do draw every new figure in `docs/assets/src/build.py` from the `THEMES` roles, and ship it as a `-light` and a `-dark` file placed with `<picture>`.
Do keep figures at the 600 measure with all lettering at 17, and the cover alone at 880.
Do use Helvetica Bold capitals for names and Courier for data, as outlines, and give each figure an `aria-label` and an `alt` that state every value it shows.
Do say in words what a marking colour means inside the figure that uses it.
Do hold checklists to 38 columns with full-stop leaders and capital responses, and put commands in their own `bash` block.
Do state conditions with every performance table, and sign each photograph or recording with its run and date.
Do begin each of the nine section headings with its thumb tab, shown at 28 by 28.
Do leave prose, tables, code blocks, links and alerts in GitHub's own styling.
donts: Don't use green, yellow or red for emphasis, decoration or status. They are data; see The Marking Code Rule.
Don't use the hatched rule or Emergency Red outside Section 3.
Don't add shadows, gradients, tints or rounded containers. Rounded corners belong only to a drawing of a rounded object.
Don't put live text or font references in an SVG, or add a second lettering size to a figure.
Don't set lettering in light-theme Caution Yellow; it is a band colour.
Don't add badges, logos, emoji bullets or a screenshot carousel, and do not use the game's logos, trade dress or interface styling.
Don't invent approvals, stamps, serial numbers or signatures. The handbook borrows the form of an aircraft manual, not its authority.
Don't add a fourth kind of notice or use an alert for anything but its defined meaning.
narrative.scope: northStar, overview, keyCharacteristics, dos and donts at this level describe the README and bind the README only. The launcher's are under narrative.launcher. In rules, each entry says which surface it binds.

launcher.overview:
The launcher is a modern game launcher and nothing else: one calm dark window, a panel with a backdrop, one bright action and one line of status under the title. It keeps the company its owner named, the RSI Launcher and CurseForge, and it refuses two things: the costume of an instrument panel, and anything a person has to read before they can press the button. A first launcher built in the handbook's style was rejected by the owner on 12 November 2026; this system replaces it for the app and leaves the README as it was.

The surface is a web page in a system web view inside a macOS window on Apple silicon: 1180 by 760 by default, never smaller than 980 by 680, dark only, with the window's title bar transparent over the page. Every token of the launcher is a value in `launcher/ui/app.css`. The named values are custom properties on `:root`; the remaining fills are written in place in that stylesheet and are named here.

It is an app someone operates, so its materials are the ordinary ones of a desktop app: the system typeface, real controls with hover, focus, pressed and disabled states, and state colours that say ready, your turn and failed. It runs beside a game that needs the whole machine, so in flight the window holds still.
keyCharacteristics: A neutral charcoal ground with three tonal layers above it, hairline borders and no drop shadows.
One blue for the action and for progress. Green, amber and red only for state, always beside words.
The system typeface in sentence case: 12, 13 and 15 for the interface, then 20, 22 and 44, each with one job.
Rounded: 10 for controls, 12 for cards and the large buttons, 14 for the hero panel.
Opaque fills on everything laid over the backdrop. No blur, no glass.
A photograph for a backdrop: one of three from NASA's open archives, or the person's own picture. Nothing drawn or generated, and no imagery or logos of the game.
Authored line icons of one weight.
In flight nothing animates and nothing transitions.
dos: Do take every launcher colour from the `launcher-` tokens, and give a new surface a named value in `launcher/ui/app.css` before using it.
Do keep one bright button on the Play page: `launcher-accent` with `launcher-on-accent` lettering, 52 high, radius 12.
Do give every control its hover, focus, pressed and disabled state, and keep the focus ring: 2 px of `launcher-accent-up`, 3 px off the control.
Do pair every state colour with words: a dot with its sentence, a coloured value with its note.
Do set changing numbers in tabular numerals, and show an en dash where there is no reading yet.
Do use the one easing, cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1), for a change of state, at 0.15 to 0.18 s, and transition only colour, transform, opacity and clip-path.
Do draw a new icon on the 20 grid with a 1.6 round stroke in the current text colour.
Do write ranges with the word "to" here as in the README, and label any reading that is simulated.
donts: Don't carry the handbook into the launcher: no Helvetica and Courier lettering, no tracked capitals, no thumb tabs, placards, dot leaders or hatching, no square ruled frames.
Don't use green, amber or red for emphasis or decoration, and don't use blue to mean good.
Don't add a second accent or a second bright button.
Don't put a translucent or blurred fill over the backdrop.
Don't use imagery, logos, trade dress or interface styling of the game.
Don't add drop shadows. A ring is an inset line of 1 px, or 1.5 px on a step mark.
Don't repeat the status sentence elsewhere on the page, and don't show a number that was not read from this Mac without saying where it was measured.
Don't animate anything while the game runs, and don't add a looping animation in any state.
Don't set the interface in monospace. The monospace face belongs to the Log page.
Don't add a size between the steps: the ramp is 12, 13, 15, 20, 22 and 44.
